question: What does rheumatism generally mean in clinical practice?

options.A: Degenerative disorders limited strictly to the spine
options.B: Acute bacterial infections of the bone marrow
options.C: Painful conditions affecting joints and muscles
options.D: Congenital malformations of the upper limbs

explanation: Rheumatism is a broad term used for various painful conditions affecting the musculoskeletal system, including joints, muscles, and bones. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T12#GNS222_U1_T12_h1)

question: Why is rheumatism considered a general term instead of a single specific diagnosis?

options.A: It describes symptoms that have no known physical cause
options.B: It covers over a hundred different musculoskeletal disorders
options.C: It only affects elderly patients in tropical regions
options.D: It represents a temporary side effect of antibiotic use

explanation: Because it includes more than a hundred distinct conditions with different causes, it acts as a general category rather than one specific diagnosis. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T12#GNS222_U1_T12_h1)

question: Which membrane inside a joint is mainly attacked during autoimmune joint inflammation?
explanation: The synovium is the inner lining of the joint capsule. Immune cells attack this area, causing local inflammation and joint damage. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T12#GNS222_U1_T12_h2)

question: What is the main effect of pannus formation in damaged joints?

options.A: It prevents systemic spread of inflammatory cytokines
options.B: It provides structural support to weak ligaments
options.C: It destroys adjacent cartilage and bone tissue
options.D: It accelerates the production of healthy synovial fluid

explanation: Pannus is abnormal tissue that grows over and destroys nearby cartilage and bone, leading to permanent joint changes. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T12#GNS222_U1_T12_h2)

question: What is the main cause behind osteoarthritis?

options.A: Mechanical wear and tear of joint cartilage
options.B: Systemic autoimmune attacks on synovial membranes
options.C: Deposition of uric acid crystals in tissues
options.D: Bacterial infection invading the joint capsule

explanation: Osteoarthritis happens mainly due to the gradual wear and tear of joint cartilage over time. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T12#GNS222_U1_T12_h3)

question: A patient has sudden, severe pain and swelling in the big toe joint. Which condition is most likely?
explanation: Gout often causes sudden, painful flare-ups in the big toe because of a buildup of uric acid crystals. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T12#GNS222_U1_T12_h3)

question: Which habit is strongly linked to a higher risk of developing rheumatoid arthritis?
explanation: Smoking tobacco is a known environmental risk factor that can interact with genes to trigger autoimmune joint inflammation. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T12#GNS222_U1_T12_h4)

question: How does obesity contribute to joint problems?

options.A: It increases mechanical load on weight-bearing joints
options.B: It prevents the absorption of essential calcium in bones
options.C: It directly destroys the immune system's white blood cells
options.D: It thickens the synovial membrane prematurely

explanation: Extra body weight places continuous physical stress on weight-bearing joints like the knees, speeding up cartilage breakdown. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T12#GNS222_U1_T12_h4)

question: Which blood test measures how fast red blood cells settle to check for inflammation?
explanation: The erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) goes up when inflammation causes red blood cells to stick together and fall faster in a test tube. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T12#GNS222_U1_T12_h5)

question: What is the main reason for performing an arthrocentesis during a joint check?

options.A: To inject permanent pain medication into the bone
options.B: To analyze synovial fluid for crystals or infection
options.C: To repair torn ligaments within the joint capsule
options.D: To measure systemic C-reactive protein levels

explanation: Arthrocentesis means drawing fluid from the joint space to test it for germs, blood, or crystals like uric acid. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T12#GNS222_U1_T12_h5)

question: What is the main goal of Disease-Modifying Anti-Rheumatic Drugs (DMARDs)?

options.A: To provide immediate relief from sharp acute pain
options.B: To dissolve calcium deposits in the bone marrow
options.C: To lower elevated blood pressure during flares
options.D: To halt progressive joint destruction and deformity

explanation: DMARDs target the immune system to slow down or stop permanent damage to the joints. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T12#GNS222_U1_T12_h6)

question: A patient with chronic knee osteoarthritis asks for a safe exercise tip to manage daily stiffness. What should the nurse suggest?

options.A: Rest the affected joint completely for several weeks
options.B: Avoid all forms of physical therapy indefinitely
options.C: Perform high-intensity running to strengthen bone
options.D: Engage in low-impact exercises like swimming

explanation: Low-impact exercises keep joints moving and build supporting muscles without putting too much stress on the cartilage. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T12#GNS222_U1_T12_h6)

question: Why is balancing rest and physical activity important in a rheumatic care plan?

options.A: It ensures the complete elimination of systemic antibodies
options.B: It cures the underlying autoimmune disorder permanently
options.C: It stops the liver from metabolizing anti-inflammatory drugs
options.D: It prevents joint contractures while avoiding excessive fatigue

explanation: Careful pacing helps stop muscle wasting and stiffness without overworking sore joints during flare-ups. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T12#GNS222_U1_T12_h7)

question: A patient with hand deformities from rheumatoid arthritis struggles to button their shirt. Which healthcare professional should the nurse consult?
explanation: Occupational therapists help patients find tools and ways to stay independent with everyday tasks like dressing. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T12#GNS222_U1_T12_h7)

question: Which long-term problem is linked to taking corticosteroids over a long period for rheumatic conditions?
explanation: Long-term use of systemic steroids interferes with normal bone upkeep, raising the risk of weak bones and fractures. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T12#GNS222_U1_T12_h8)

question: What is the main goal of a rehabilitation program for patients with chronic joint diseases?

options.A: To completely reverse existing permanent bone deformities
options.B: To prevent the development of unrelated infectious diseases
options.C: To eliminate the need for any future medical follow-ups
options.D: To restore maximum functional independence and quality of life

explanation: Rehab helps patients adapt to physical changes, make the most of their abilities, and live as independently as possible. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T12#GNS222_U1_T12_h8)
